::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 10th [1881]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Charlotte Mitchell.
:::

My dear [Edith](people/person_749.qmd)

Would this be the kind of thing?[^1]  I suspect it is too long.  It is a beginning I once made and you may as well look at it.  I also send a paper on the study of the Bible, which an American Sunday School Society once made me write and which might serve you some day perhaps.

You see this is a mere beginning, hardly getting beyond the Acts.  [Canon Bright](people/person_199.qmd) wanted me to do a Church history, and I got so far and then quailed - wanting the lash of a serial to keep me up to it.

We seem to be getting on well under the new dynasty, but it has been a strange thing that in one spring the school should lose Vicar, master and pupil teacher[^2]

your affectionate

CMYonge

I was going to cut out the article but on second thoughts I send the whole paper as there are curious things in it

&nbsp;

---

[^1]: CMY has evidently been asked for a contribution to [The Watchword](organizations/other_100.qmd), the periodical edited by Edith Jacob which circulated among the [Society of Watchers and Workers](organizations/other_47.qmd).  She certainly contributed a series 'Militant Here on Earth' about the early history of the church which deals with the travels of St. Paul and might be the article referred to.
[^2]: [The Rev. Walter Elgie](people/person_478.qmd), Vicar of Otterbourne, died in February 1881 and was succeeded by the [Rev. Walter Brock](people/person_201.qmd). A week after his arrival the schoolmaster, [Walter Fisher](people/person_513.qmd), also died.
